news.headline: Wells Fargo Lifts uniQure Target to $75 as Wall Street's Post-Earnings Price-Target Wave Continues
news.summary: Wells Fargo raised its uniQure price target to $75 from $60 while maintaining an Overweight rating, joining a broader wave of post-Q2-earnings upgrades that also saw Chardan Capital lift its target to $76 and Cantor Fitzgerald to $80. The moves follow Wolfe Research's July 29 upgrade to Outperform and add to a string of target hikes (Leerink to $70, Mizuho to $68, Goldman Sachs to $46) as analysts grow more confident in AMT-130's regulatory and commercial prospects.

news.headline: uniQure Reports Q2 2026 Financial Results: AMT-130 BLA on Track, $259M Offering Extends Cash Runway Into 2030
news.summary: uniQure posted Q2 2026 revenue of $5.8 million (up from $5.3 million a year earlier) and a net loss of $81.1 million, or $1.22 per share. The company ended the quarter with $810.3 million in cash after its June offering and confirmed both the US BLA and UK MHRA marketing authorization application for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease remain on track for submission in Q3 2026, with runway now extending into 2030.

news.headline: uniQure CMO Signals FDA Advisory Committee Likely for AMT-130
news.summary: On the Q2 earnings call, chief medical officer Walid Abi-Saab said an FDA advisory committee meeting is likely for AMT-130 since it would be the first gene therapy for Huntington's disease, and that the company is preparing for one. uniQure also reiterated plans to present four-year follow-up data on all 24 patients from the first two AMT-130 dosing cohorts in September 2026.

news.headline: uniQure Closes $259 Million Upsized Public Offering
news.summary: uniQure closed an upsized public offering of 5,686,813 ordinary shares at $45.50 per share, including full exercise of the underwriters' option, for gross proceeds of $259 million. Proceeds are earmarked for AMT-130 commercialization readiness, a required confirmatory study, other pipeline programs, and general corporate purposes.

news.headline: uniQure Reports Preliminary AMT-260 Phase I/IIa Low-Dose Data: 3 of 6 Epilepsy Patients Show 79-100% Seizure Reduction
news.summary: At the Epilepsy Foundation Pipeline Conference, uniQure presented six-month follow-up data on the first, low-dose cohort of its AMT-260 gene therapy for refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, with three of six patients showing 79-100% reductions in disabling seizures and no serious treatment-related adverse events. Enrollment continues in a higher-dose cohort, with updated results expected in the first half of 2027.

news.headline: uniQure Shares Surge 78% After FDA Reverses Course, Backs 3-Year AMT-130 Data for Accelerated Approval
news.summary: uniQure stock soared roughly 78% after the company disclosed that the FDA reversed a prior negative stance and agreed that its existing 3-year AMT-130 Phase I/II data, benchmarked against external controls, can support a Biologics License Application under the accelerated approval pathway. This reopened a path to a Q3 2026 BLA submission after the FDA had pushed back on external-control comparisons as recently as November 2025.

catalysts.label: FDA BLA submission for AMT-130
catalysts.detail: uniQure remains on track to submit a Biologics License Application seeking accelerated approval of AMT-130 for Huntington's disease, following FDA agreement that 3-year Phase I/II data can support the filing; not yet submitted as of the July 29 earnings update.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA marketing authorization application for AMT-130
catalysts.detail: In parallel with the US filing, uniQure plans to submit a Marketing Authorization Application to the UK's MHRA for AMT-130, following a successful pre-submission meeting.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 four-year Phase I/II data presentation
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to present four-year follow-up safety and efficacy data on all 24 patients (12 high-dose, 12 low-dose) from the first two AMT-130 dosing cohorts in the Huntington's disease program.

catalysts.label: FDA Advisory Committee (AdCom) meeting for AMT-130
catalysts.detail: uniQure's chief medical officer said an FDA advisory committee meeting is likely for AMT-130 given it would be the first Huntington's disease gene therapy, and the company is preparing for one; no date has been set.

catalysts.label: Confirmatory study design alignment with FDA
catalysts.detail: uniQure is finalizing with the FDA the design of the required post-approval confirmatory study for AMT-130, including consideration of a randomized standard-of-care control arm instead of a sham-surgery control.

catalysts.label: Updated AMT-260 Phase I/IIa epilepsy data readout
catalysts.detail: uniQure expects to present updated safety and efficacy results, including higher-dose cohort data, from the ongoing AMT-260 refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy trial.

pulse: uniQure remains in rally mode heading into the end of July 2026, building on the roughly 78% single-day surge triggered by the FDA's June 17 reversal that cleared 3-year AMT-130 data to support an accelerated-approval BLA for Huntington's disease. Q2 2026 results on July 29 (revenue $5.8M, cash of $810.3M after the June $259M offering, runway into 2030) confirmed both the US BLA and UK MHRA filings remain on track for Q3 2026, with four-year data due in September 2026 and an FDA advisory committee meeting now considered likely; the print triggered a fresh wave of Wall Street price-target hikes, with Wells Fargo, Chardan Capital and Cantor Fitzgerald all raising targets into the $75-80 range on July 30-31 alongside Wolfe Research's upgrade to Outperform. Early, mixed-but-promising AMT-260 epilepsy data adds a second pipeline catalyst, though the stock still trades meaningfully below most analysts' targets, reflecting lingering uncertainty over the AdCom and confirmatory-study design ahead of the actual BLA filing.
